title: Where does this decision reach?
subject: PR #131 · Route daemon thresholds through centralized policy

decisions.title: One output slice governs capture and retention
decisions.summary: Remove local inline, record, per-result and aggregate limits. Pass the same output slice into command capture and completion spooling, including disk decoding.

reason.text: Required slices prevent an omitted input from recreating a local default.

before: Capture and spool each supply fallback limits.
Disk decoding assumes a fixed 64 KiB record.
after: Composition supplies output policy to both stores.
The record cap travels into stored-file decoding.
decisions.numbers: 64 KiB per chunk · 256 KiB inline · 256 MiB per result · 512 MiB aggregate spool

decisions.title: Carry chunk and frame caps through each validator
decisions.summary: Transport, binary codec, file reader and both worker-message endpoints use supplied caps. JSON and execution-control limits stay separate; the worker host decodes the snapshot to recover its chunk cap.

reason.text: The PR explicitly includes framing and worker chunk validation in required output/resource consumption. The policy record distinguishes ordinary JSON from transfer control frames.

before: Spool exports a 64 KiB chunk constant.
Transport and codec import local frame/chunk constants.
after: Transport supplies chunk limits to encode/decode.
Worker sender and receiver validate against the snapshot.

evidence.label: Binary capacity = control allowance + raw chunk allowance
Worker host reads the serialized cap

decisions.numbers: 8 MiB JSON · 256 KiB execution control · 64 KiB raw chunk

decisions.title: Use snapshot memory values without a second derivation
decisions.summary: Delete the CLI resource-policy class and memory-cap input. The snapshot now supplies RSS thresholds, reported hard cap, worker heap limit, supervision and heap-sampling cadence, and the replacement circuit.

reason.text: All numeric limits have one owner; consumers must not reconstruct the policy.

before: DaemonResourcePolicy re-derives a CLI resource record.
WorkspaceDaemon can rebuild it from a memory cap.
after: WorkspaceDaemon uses policy.values.resources directly.
Supervisor and worker sampling consume the recorded cadence and replacement limits.
decisions.numbers: 250 ms supervision · 25 ms heap sampling · 2 replacements per 10 min; next pressure event drains

decisions.title: Keep startup coordination separate from healthy warm-up
decisions.summary: Supply registry grace, heartbeat, authorization polling, readiness polling and old-process termination through policy. Remove the unused startup-timeout member and test knob; progressing warm-up remains unbounded.

reason.text: The policy record gives coordination a recovery grace and deliberately gives healthy startup no project-size deadline.
reason.source: plans/005/daemon-policy.md · Startup rows and intentional absences

before: Registry uses a 15 s constant; coordinator carries an unused startupTimeoutMs field.
Heartbeat and authorization waits are local numbers.
after: Coordination grace belongs to startup policy.
Heartbeat, polling and previous-instance termination receive distinct policy values; no healthy warm-up timer is introduced.
decisions.numbers: 15 s grace · 100 ms heartbeat · 10 ms authorization · 20 ms observation · 5 min previous-process termination

decisions.title: Keep distinct stop, idle and acknowledgement clocks
decisions.summary: Require shutdown policy for idle lifetime, controller stop, signal waits and drain acknowledgements. Preserve the half-window bound on forced-stop reserve and the fast acknowledgement poll.

reason.text: The policy record assigns separate reasons to idle cleanup, bounded stop, signal exit and acknowledgement grace.

before: Idle constant plus local stop, signal and acknowledgement numbers.
Force reserve is min(500 ms, half the stop window).
after: Each consumer receives its required shutdown values.
Force reserve keeps the same formula with the policy maximum.
decisions.numbers: 30 min idle · 5 s stop · ≤500 ms force reserve · 500 ms per signal · 250 ms acknowledgement grace / 5 ms poll

decisions.title: Policy owns both diagnostic storage limits
decisions.summary: Logger rotation, backup count and queue capacity use diagnostics policy. Disconnected operation traces use its retention and capacity, keeping an effective minimum of one trace; completion retention is a separate mechanism.

reason.text: Log size/history and slow-storage queues are bounded; disconnected traces retain reconnect evidence independently of results.

before: Logger has constants and optional queue/rotation overrides.
WorkspaceDaemon carries optional trace retention knobs.
after: A required diagnostics slice configures the logger.
WorkspaceDaemon reads trace limits from the same snapshot.

evidence.label: Backup count now comes from policy

decisions.numbers: 10 MiB log · 4 backups · 1,024 queued events · 5 min / 1,024 disconnected traces (minimum 1)

decisions.title: Choose a response deadline by composition purpose
decisions.summary: Status aggregation explicitly selects status-observer (100 ms); ordinary lifecycle and execution-status requests retain 250 ms. Admission still has 5 s, and accepted completion has no time deadline.

reason.text: Status observation and ordinary execution-status requests have distinct deadlines; request kind does not express who is observing.

before: Status action creates a transport with requestTimeoutMs: 100.
Other transports fall back to 250 ms.
after: Status action selects responseTimeoutPurpose: status-observer.
Transport projects that purpose into a policy value; admission remains separate.

evidence.needle: it("uses the ordinary timeout for execution-status exchanges"
evidence.label: Characterization uses an ordinary transport

decisions.numbers: 100 ms observer · 250 ms ordinary · 5 s admission · no accepted-completion deadline

decisions.title: Give execute reattachment and result fetch separate budgets
decisions.summary: Replace the fixed reattachment wrapper and fetch boolean with independent numeric counters. Every execute attempt owns a fresh fetch counter; fetch failure still goes directly to failure handling.

reason.text: Each reattached execute attempt has its own fetch-resume allowance.

before: One fixed reattachment wrapper.
One resumeStarted boolean inside each execute attempt.
after: Outer loop counts accepted-execution reattachments.
Each executeOnce owns resumeCount; its fetch rejection calls fail.
flow: Attempt A · its own fetch counter
Attempt B · a fresh fetch counter

evidence.label: Fetch guard and terminal rejection path

evidence.needle: it("gives the reattached execute attempt its own fetch resume"
evidence.label: Added scenario: 2 execute connections and 1 fetch

decisions.numbers: Default: 1 reattachment · 1 fetch resume per execution attempt

decisions.title: Count startup retries for explicit child failure
decisions.summary: Replace the fixed second launch with a loop bounded by childFailureRetryLimit. Only child-exit or lost-warm-up errors consume it; tests add zero- and two-retry policies.

reason.text: The default preserves one fresh launch after a failed child.

before: Catch an eligible failure and call triggerAndWait once more.
after: Count eligible failures, retry while policy allows, otherwise rethrow.

evidence.needle: it("does not retry a child failure when policy permits zero retries"
evidence.label: Zero retry scenario

evidence.needle: it("allows each child-failure retry granted by policy"
evidence.label: Two retry scenario

decisions.title: Move legacy test knobs into seven test-only adapters
decisions.summary: Tests import adapter subclasses or a resource adapter that builds validated policy. Runtime constructors require policy; test clocks, storage, process and worker seams still exist.

reason.text: Tests need small thresholds without restoring runtime tuning seams.

before: Tests construct production mechanisms with optional numeric knobs.
after: Test adapters translate old inputs through DaemonPolicyTestFactory.
Production constructors receive required policy; non-threshold seams remain.

evidence.label: Resource compatibility delegates to the central owner

decisions.baseline: The seven adapter symbols are new in head; base has no corresponding adapter surface.

decisions.title: Adjust small test policies and their storage paths
decisions.summary: Valid policies require positive chunks ≤ inline ≤ result ≤ aggregate. Tests replace inline=0 and rescale chunk/inline values; adapters clamp inline, create output directories, and accept a legacy memoryCapBytes value that they do not project.

reason.text: The general adapter strategy is stated. No separate reason is recorded for these particular input translations, directory creation or retained-but-unprojected memoryCapBytes.
reason.source: No reason found in the supplied PR body, commit messages, or policy/architecture records.

before: Fixtures can force immediate disk storage with inline=0.
Caller-provided small limits need not form a valid snapshot.
after: Fixtures select ordered positive limits; some storage paths change.
Transport adapter raises inline to at least the chunk cap and creates its directory.
Workspace adapter remaps zero inline when a result cap exists; memoryCapBytes remains accepted without projection.

evidence.label: Legacy accepted memory-cap option; full adapter available in file evidence
Aggregate-cap fixture now keeps first six bytes inline

decisions.baseline: These adapter symbols are new; their reach measures test consumers, not the storage behavior exercised.

decisions.title: Remove the CLI resource-derivation test block
decisions.summary: The deleted block covers five memory sizes, constraint selection and the 250 ms constant. Central policy tests already cover related derivation/default cases; the exact old 256 MiB table row is absent there.

reason.text: Removing the old owner is stated; no specific reason for deleting these assertions or selecting the replacement case set was found.
reason.source: No reason found in the supplied PR body, commit messages, or policy/architecture records.

before: CLI tests pin five memory inputs, two constraint choices and a constant.
after: The local derivation block is removed.
Existing package tests pin default values, memory recipes and constraints; their input table includes 1 byte instead of the old 256 MiB case.

evidence.needle: it("uses the required resource-policy cadence and thresholds"
evidence.label: New consumer characterization

decisions.unmeasured: Assertion coverage is not a referenced symbol. No numeric radius is assigned.

decisions.title: Use policy-based expectations and cast new fixtures
decisions.summary: Spool/e2e expectations now read policy defaults instead of retired constants. Three added policy-consumer cases cast through unknown to constructor parameter types, so those fixtures bypass normal assignability checks.

reason.text: No reason found for the casts in the added spool, logger and supervisor cases. Replacing retired constant imports follows the stated migration, but the effect on test independence is not discussed.
reason.source: No reason found in the supplied PR body, commit messages, or policy/architecture records.

before: Capacity assertions compare against production constants.
after: Capacity assertions compare against the policy provider.
New override tests exercise runtime values using casts that bypass ordinary fixture type checking.

evidence.label: E2E expected values use the policy

decisions.unmeasured: A type-checking or test-oracle choice has no stable symbol-ref footprint.

decisions.title: Enforce retirement with a production-source string scan
decisions.summary: Extend the package meta-test to reject old constant names, optional threshold seams and local policy reconstruction identifiers. This encodes a source boundary through strings; it does not trace semantic data flow.

reason.text: Required slices and test-only adapters must not restore local ownership or bypasses. The PR explicitly calls out the retired-default rejection test.
reason.source: PR body · Where it lives and Decisions

before: The meta-test rejects three optional/reconstructed DaemonPolicy forms.
after: The same scan rejects the retired defaults and bypass names across app production source.

evidence.needle: it("retires scattered operational defaults and policy bypasses"
evidence.label: Expanded boundary scan

decisions.unmeasured: String-based source rules are invisible to symbol references.

decisions.title: Let a later completion failure become the reported error
decisions.summary: The new reattachment loop propagates the current completion failure when its budget is exhausted. A failure to obtain the reattachment receipt still preserves the preceding error. This is not called out in the PR.

reason.text: The PR explains numeric retry budgets, but gives no reason for changing which completion error escapes the wrapper.
reason.source: No reason found in the supplied PR body, commit messages, or policy/architecture records.

before: The nested reattachment catch rethrows the original first error, including when the reattached completion rejects.
after: Later completion rejection is handled by the next loop iteration.
Failed receipt acquisition still rethrows the error that initiated that reattachment.
flow: Completion B fails at exhausted budget
